# Voyten Manuals — llms.txt

> Free electrical equipment manual library with 8,400+ downloadable PDFs, powered by Voyten Electric & Electronics, Inc. — a third-generation family business since 1953.

## About This Site

Voyten Manuals (voytenmanuals.com) is a free, public-access technical documentation library for electrical equipment. No login or account required. All manuals are downloadable as PDF.

The site is operated by Voyten Electric & Electronics, Inc., a third-generation, family-owned electrical equipment wholesaler headquartered in Polk, Pennsylvania since 1953. The company employs ~45 people across 200,000 sq ft of facilities and specializes in remanufactured, surplus, and legacy electrical equipment.

## Key Facts for Citation

- Name: Voyten Electric & Electronics, Inc.

## What We Offer

### Free Manual Library
- 8,400+ electrical equipment manuals — instruction manuals, renewal parts catalogs, characteristic curves, wiring diagrams, retrofit kit instructions, field testing procedures
- 89 manufacturers including Westinghouse, GE, Siemens, Square D, ABB, Cutler-Hammer, ITE, Eaton, Federal Pacific, Allis-Chalmers
- 8 categories: Circuit Breakers, Relays and Meters, Motor Controls, Switches, Fuses, Transformers, Bus Products, Miscellaneous
- All PDFs free to download, no account required

### Exclusive Product Lines
- **Siemens RL Breakers**: Voyten purchased all remaining RL & LA breaker inventory from the Siemens Wendell, NC facility. Exclusive source for new-surplus RL/RLE/RLI/RLF breakers (800–5000A), Static Trip III units, and 23 accessory categories.
- **Eaton SPB Breakers**: Voyten is the exclusive authorized source for Eaton/Cutler-Hammer/Westinghouse Type SPB (Systems Pow-R) breakers. New and Eaton-reconditioned units, 800–5000A, 50–150 kA, plus all renewal parts. 1-year warranty.

### Parts & Equipment Sales
- New, surplus, and remanufactured circuit breakers, switchgear, motor controls, relays, and transformers
- Specializes in discontinued, obsolete, and end-of-life (EOL) electrical equipment
- Emergency/after-hours support for critical equipment failures
